problem_definition.packed_cbor: Packed CBOR (draft-ietf-cbor-packed) uses two optimization tables: (1) item sharing (structure sharing), where repeated substructures are replaced by references, and (2) argument sharing (prefix/suffix sharing), where strings or containers sharing common affixes are replaced by a reference to the shared argument plus a 'rump' remainder.
problem_definition.optimal_packing: The problem of minimizing Packed CBOR output size is: given a CBOR data item, choose a set of entries for the shared-item table and the argument table, and replace occurrences of repeated items/affixes with references, to minimize the total encoded size.

np_hardness.status: NP-hard (inferred from related problems; no published paper proves this specifically for CBOR)

evidence.result: NP-complete (decision version); APX-hard with inapproximability ratio 8569/8568
evidence.reduction: From Vertex Cover on degree-3 graphs. Charikar et al. construct a string from a graph such that the smallest grammar size equals 15|V| + 3|E| + k, where k is the minimum vertex cover size.

evidence.reduction: Storer & Szymanski's External Pointer Macro (EPM) and Copying Macro (CPM) models. Finding the minimum macro scheme is NP-complete even with restrictions.

evidence.result: NP-complete for k >= 3; APX-complete for constant k; NP-complete for k=2 (recently settled)
evidence.reduction: From k-Set Cover. A string attractor is a set of positions capturing all distinct substrings; dictionary compressors (SLPs, LZ77, macro schemes) are approximations of the minimum attractor.

reduction_to_packed_cbor.description: Packed CBOR's two-table scheme combines item sharing (equivalent to straight-line programs / smallest grammar) and argument sharing (equivalent to macro schemes / string attractors). Since both sub-problems are NP-hard, the combined problem is NP-hard. Specifically: (1) Item sharing without argument sharing reduces to the Smallest Grammar Problem on the tree-structured CBOR data. (2) Argument sharing on strings without item sharing reduces to the Smallest Macro Scheme problem. (3) The combined optimization requires choosing which items to place in both tables simultaneously to minimize total size, which is at least as hard as either sub-problem.
reduction_to_packed_cbor.note: No published paper explicitly proves 'Packed CBOR optimal packing is NP-hard.' The IETF draft states: 'Different packers can differ in the amount of effort they invest in arriving at a reduced-redundancy packed form.' This is a deliberate design choice: the format is decoupled from the packing algorithm.

greedy_packing.bound: O(log(n/g*)) where g* is the size of the smallest grammar
greedy_packing.proof_technique: Based on LZ77-style parsing. The greedy algorithm builds a balanced binary grammar from an LZ77-style factorization. Each LZ77 phrase of length l is encoded with O(log l) grammar rules. Since the number of phrases s <= g* and total length is n, the grammar size is O(sum log(l_i)) = O(s log(n/s)) = O(g* log(n/g*)).

citation.authors: Moses Charikar, Eric Lehman, Ding Liu, Rina Panigrahy, Manoj Prabhakaran, April Rasala, Amit Sahai, Abhi Shelat
citation.title: Approximating the Smallest Grammar: Kolmogorov Complexity in Natural Models

rytter_algorithm.bound: O(log(n/m*)) where m* is the optimal grammar size
rytter_algorithm.description: Independently discovered by Rytter (2003). Uses a variant of LZ77 with balanced binary grammar construction. Achieves the same asymptotic bound.

citation.author: Wojciech Rytter
citation.title: Application of Lempel-Ziv factorization to the approximation of grammar-based compression

greedy_grammar_lower_bound.bound: Omega(log n / log log n) lower bound for any polynomial-time grammar compressor unless P=NP (connection to addition chains)
greedy_grammar_lower_bound.description: Charikar et al. show that improving the approximation ratio to o(log n / log log n) would require progress on the addition chain problem.

citation.reference: Same as Charikar et al. 2005 (IEEE Trans. IT), Theorem 2

string_attractor_approximation.bound: O(log k) approximation for k-attractor via reduction to Set Cover

greedy_for_packed_cbor.note: No specific approximation ratio analysis exists for greedy Packed CBOR packing. By analogy with grammar-based compression, a greedy strategy that repeatedly replaces the most-frequent repeated substring/prefix with a table entry achieves O(log(n/g*)) approximation. The IETF draft notes that 'often, they simply employ the sharing that is natural for a specific application.'

open_problems: Whether optimal Packed CBOR packing is NP-hard remains unpublished as a formal result, though it follows trivially from the NP-hardness of the Smallest Grammar Problem and Smallest Macro Scheme Problem.
The exact inapproximability threshold for the Smallest Grammar Problem is unknown: gap between 8569/8568 approx 1.0001 lower bound and O(log(n/g*)) upper bound.
Whether a constant-factor approximation exists for the Smallest Grammar Problem is open (equivalent to membership in APX).
The complexity of optimal pair encoding (BPE) with fixed alphabet is open (APX-hard for unbounded alphabet, but fixed alphabet case is open).
